newsitem.title: USA: US cash crudes mixed amid scattered short-covering.
newsitem.headline: US cash crudes mixed amid scattered short-covering.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes were mixed amid scattered short-covering coinciding with the NYMEX front-month contract expiry, traders said.
The July NYMEX crude contract expired on Friday afternoon at $18.55 a barrel, down 12 cents from Thursday.
Cash West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was running around five cents ahead of the future price at $18.55-65, factoring in a five cent premium for exchange-for-physical (EFPs) deals.
July EFPs were done at plus four, five and six cents a barrel over the day. In recent weeks, the deals have gone for as high as 25 cents amid concerns over foreign crude deliveries into the NYMEX.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James came off from earlier in the day to talk around minus two to plus two cents a barrel. The grade traded between flat and plus seven cents.
WTI/Midland was firmer at WTI/Cushing minus 32-30 cents, having moved at minus 33, 37 and 38 cents.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was wide at minus 45-30 cents, and was last traded at minus 42 cents.
Sour continued to show strength on short-covering and uncertainty over the timing of Iraqi exports.
West Texas Sour/Midland climbed to $1.05 to 95 cents under WTI/Cushing, up 10-20 cents from late on Thursday. The grade traded over the day at between $1.00 and $1.10 discount.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus continued to sink in line with the spread, reaching $1.66-68 a barrel, down two cents from early afternoon.
